I've been farming this land for 15 years and I know the rhythm of Quzhou well. My 1.5 mu runs the standard winter wheat into summer maize rotation — the whole plot goes to wheat in winter, then immediately flips to maize after harvest. With some family off-farm, I don't need to maximize every jin, but I'm not going to leave yield on the table either. I have well irrigation, which is my main edge over dryland farmers here, especially for wheat in the dry spring.

**For wheat:** I'll plant Kenong 199 — it's proven here, good resistance to stripe rust and powdery mildew, stable yield. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest to work in the stover. Base fertilizer goes in at planting: full phosphorus and potassium, plus a third of nitrogen. I'll topdress the rest of the nitrogen at jointing. Irrigation: pre-winter to ensure good tillering, then jointing, then heading — three times is usually enough with winter rain. I'll spray herbicide early spring for broadleaf weeds and do a fungicide + insecticide pass at heading for aphids and rust. Aiming for 450 kg/mu.

**For maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed Xianyu 335 — no-till to save time and keep moisture. I'll apply compound fertilizer at sowing, then chase with urea at the V6-V8 stage. Summer rains usually do the heavy lifting but I'll irrigate once if August is dry. One post-emergence herbicide pass and one insecticide for corn borer. Targeting 600 kg/mu.
